Years ago, MacBook featured a security lock slot that let you tether the laptop to a desk leg or similar object. These slots were particularly handy in cafés — when you headed to the counter to grab another drink, you didn't have to carry your laptop around with you.

Those slots long disappeared, but you can now buy adapters that let you attach a cable lock to a MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro……

If you remember the security lock slot on the side of the machine, you've probably been using MacBooks for quite some time. The slot was originally designed to accept a T-shaped lock, which you would insert and then rotate 90 degrees to secure. The most common design involved a steel cable that could be looped around a café or library table leg.

CompuLock has recently brought this concept back to market, launching adapters that mount to the corner or edge of a MacBook, allowing you to connect a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design, with screws used to secure the bracket to the MacBook.

The company has now added a model for the MacBook Neo, having previously offered versions for the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro.

It's worth emphasising that these locks have always been extremely low-security devices, designed only to prevent someone from grabbing your MacBook and walking off in the few seconds you step away. In a small café, I can still see my table when I pop up to the counter for a refill, so using one is fine; but if I were leaving the MacBook completely out of sight, I absolutely would not rely on it.

These adapters retail for US$70, which is not exactly cheap, and on top of that you still need to buy the lock itself separately. But if you've got a spare lock sitting in a drawer, it might be worth giving it a new lease of life.
